rv3-000113.passageAppend: The library also discovered that the mixed system affected behavior outside the desks themselves. Students who knew they had a reserved period were less likely to arrive extremely early just to protect a seat. At the same time, some long-term users became more willing to choose quiet hours because the public display showed when demand was usually lower. Staff added a simple weekly chart rather than a live crowd meter, since they did not want visitors to feel constantly monitored. Nao noticed that the best improvement came not from controlling people more strongly but from giving them clearer choices. When users could see that different kinds of space existed for different kinds of work, conflicts became easier to discuss. The library still received complaints, yet those complaints became more specific: users could say whether they needed longer sessions, more reserved seats, or better information. Specific problems were easier to test than a general statement that the library was always crowded.
rv3-000113.translationAppend: 図書館は、混合方式が机以外の行動にも影響することに気づきました。予約時間があることで席取りのため極端に早く来る必要が減り、混雑の少ない時間帯を示す週ごとの表も利用者の選択を助けました。常時監視されている印象を避けるため、リアルタイム表示にはしませんでした。奈緒は、強い規制よりも選択肢を明確にしたことが効果的だったと気づきます。『混んでいる』という曖昧な不満も、長時間席、予約席、情報不足など具体的な問題に分かれ、試しやすくなりました。

rv3-000114.passageAppend: After the demonstration, the team tested the program with people who had not helped build it. Their comments exposed another weakness. The labels easiest and safest sounded objective even though each mode depended on selected data and weighting choices. The team changed the labels to fewer stairs, more signal crossings, and shortest distance so users could see what was actually being optimized. They also added a small note when information about lighting or construction was old. Jun learned that interface words can hide assumptions just as easily as formulas can. A friendly button may make a complicated judgment look natural and unquestionable. By describing the criteria directly, the program became slightly less elegant but more transparent. Users were able to disagree with a route for a clear reason and choose another mode. The project taught Jun that a responsible algorithm should not only produce an answer efficiently. It should also help people understand enough about the answer to decide whether it fits their situation.
rv3-000114.translationAppend: 班は開発に関わっていない人にもアプリを試してもらい、『最も楽』『最も安全』という表示が客観的すぎることに気づきました。そこで『階段が少ない』『信号のある横断が多い』『距離が最短』など、実際に何を優先しているかが分かる名前に変更しました。古い情報にも注記を付けました。潤は、数式だけでなく画面の言葉も前提を隠すことがあると学びました。責任あるアルゴリズムは答えを速く出すだけでなく、その答えが自分に合うか利用者が判断できるだけの説明も必要です。

rv3-000115.passageAppend: The planning team later asked whether donations themselves could create a new problem. If a few large sponsors supplied most of the money, those sponsors might expect more influence over the program. The organizers therefore wrote a policy separating financial support from decisions about performers. They also published a short budget summary after the event so residents could see how public funds and donations were used. Maho found that transparency changed conversations. Instead of saying the festival costs too much, people could discuss particular expenses such as security, toilets, or stage equipment. Some costs that looked high at first were connected to legal or safety requirements and could not simply be removed. Other expenses were traditions that could be reconsidered. The team still had to make value judgments, but the debate became more concrete. Maho realized that understanding cost does not force a community to choose the cheapest option. It allows people to know what they are giving up when they choose something more expensive.
rv3-000115.translationAppend: 企画チームは、少数の大口スポンサーに頼ると出演内容への影響を求められる可能性も検討しました。そこで寄付と出演者決定を分ける方針を明文化し、終了後には公費と寄付の使途を示す簡単な予算報告も公開しました。すると『高すぎる』という漠然とした議論より、警備、トイレ、舞台など個別費用について話しやすくなりました。費用を理解することは最安案を選ぶことではなく、より高い案を選ぶなら何を得て何を諦めるのかを分かるようにすることだと真帆は理解しました。

rv3-000116.passageAppend: Several months after construction, Emi returned to interview the same residents. The flexible pavement was working well, but fallen leaves collected near the redirected section and became slippery after rain. The city added a different cleaning schedule. This small problem reminded Emi that compromise does not end when a meeting ends. A decision creates a new situation that also needs attention. She also noticed that some residents who had strongly opposed one another now described the process more calmly because they had seen their concerns acknowledged in the final plan. They had not changed all their values; they had gained trust that the process could respond to evidence. Emi wrote that compromise should not mean splitting every difference exactly in half. In this case, the solution protected the tree, changed parking, improved lighting, and altered maintenance in different ways. What mattered was whether the strongest concerns were addressed with reasons people could examine.
rv3-000116.translationAppend: 工事から数か月後、恵美が再び住民に聞くと、新しい歩道は機能していましたが、曲げた部分に落ち葉がたまり雨の日に滑りやすいという新問題が出ていました。市は清掃頻度を変えました。恵美は、妥協は会議で終わらず、その決定が作る新しい状況も見続ける必要があると学びました。また、妥協とは常に半分ずつ譲ることではなく、木、駐車、安全、費用など異なる重要事項へ理由を持って対応することだと理解しました。

rv3-000117.passageAppend: Saki later experimented with timing. She discovered that trying to recall material immediately after reading was useful, but trying again after a longer gap revealed different weaknesses. Some ideas that felt easy on Monday were difficult by Thursday. She began scheduling short reviews across several days rather than repeating the same chapter many times in one evening. Leo reminded her that forgetting was not simply failure; it created an opportunity to strengthen retrieval when she tried again. Saki also became more careful about confidence. Before checking an answer, she wrote how certain she felt. Sometimes she was highly confident and wrong, which was especially valuable because it showed a misunderstanding she might otherwise have kept. Her studying became less focused on producing a feeling of fluency and more focused on collecting evidence about what she could explain, remember, and apply after time had passed.
rv3-000117.translationAppend: 咲は復習の間隔も試しました。読んだ直後だけでなく数日後に思い出そうとすると、月曜日には簡単だった内容が木曜日には難しくなることがあります。同じ章を一晩で何度も見るより、数日に分けて短く思い出す練習をしました。さらに答えを見る前に自信度も記録し、『自信があるのに間違っている』内容を重要な誤解として見つけました。勉強は分かった気分を作ることより、時間がたっても説明・想起・応用できるかという証拠を集める活動へ変わりました。

rv3-000118.passageAppend: The group later compared its records with information from a neighboring beach. The two places looked similar, but their waste patterns were different because one was closer to a river mouth and the other to a busy harbor. Kenta saw why copying a successful program from another town without checking local causes could waste effort. The refill station made sense where visitors produced many drink bottles, while damaged fishing gear required cooperation with people working at sea. The volunteers began setting separate goals for different categories instead of using only total bag weight. This made progress less dramatic but more informative. A storm could still bring a huge amount of debris, yet the group could ask whether locally preventable items were changing. Kenta learned that a useful environmental measure should connect closely to an action people can actually influence. Otherwise, a number may rise or fall for reasons that have little to do with the program being judged.
rv3-000118.translationAppend: 隣の海岸の記録と比べると、見た目が似た場所でも河口や港との位置関係によりごみの種類が違いました。他地域で成功した対策を原因確認なしにコピーしても効かない場合があります。観光客の飲料容器には給水設備、漁具には海で働く人との協力というように対策を分け、総ごみ重量だけでなく種類別の目標を置きました。嵐で総量が増えても、地域で減らせるごみがどう変化しているかを見られるようになったのです。
